item.title: Climate volatility at Winter Olympics highlights risks to Asia supply chains
item.description: Extreme weather and rising emissions exposure threaten manufacturing hubs as firms face mounting costs and disruption.

item.title: National data repository must help Malaysia with local climate adaptation, say policymakers
item.description: A lack of actionable data at a local level could be addressed under the country's highly-anticipated Climate Change Bill. The environment ministry is also studying the need for regular climate change risk assessments.

item.title: We don't want others to take advantage of Asean's rich mineral resources: Philippine environment policymaker
item.description: Critical minerals will be central to this year’s Asean meetings, said environment assistant secretary Noralene Uy, as the Philippines ushers the region towards domestic processing as summit chair.

item.title: Singapore's response to AI risks will fail unless businesses and investors follow
item.description: AI promises productivity gains, but without corporate and investor commitment, Singapore risks deeper inequality, higher emissions, and growing social strain as jobs are lost.

item.title: Thailand tests AI-powered sensors to identify sources of toxic PM2.5 haze
item.description: National science agency rolls out “e-Nose” devices to guide targeted enforcement and air-quality policy.

item.title: Malaysia intercepts over 186,000 kg of illegal e-waste amid import ban
item.description: The shipment are said to be over RM2.15 million (US$550,000) in value and found to be entering the country from Canada, Spain and Croatia, being falsely declared as copper concentrate.

item.title: Asian seafood giants step up traceability, but progress to curb destructive fishing remains slow
item.description: Despite rising commitments from Japan and Thailand’s seafood companies, few firms have implemented the robust traceability systems required to manage escalating environmental and social risks, an investor assessment finds.

item.title: World Bank set to approve proposed $270 million water and sanitation projects in the Philippines
item.description: The loan is focused on investment in top tourist draws like Bohol and Siargao Island, which also suffer from strained water supply, according to the bank’s project brief.

item.title: Fukushima town launches rice-based carbon credit project under Japan’s J-Credit scheme
item.description: Local farmers will extend paddy drainage and adopt low-emission methods to generate government-certified J-Credits, creating a new revenue stream from climate-friendly rice cultivation.

item.title: China’s Belt and Road must adapt to survive a hotter world
item.description: Development projects globally must answer a burning question as rising temperatures threaten workers’ health and productivity, write three academics.
